surprises: MY OWN TEST STUB ENCODED THE SAME WRONG ASSUMPTION AS MY CODE, and that is the strongest control result of this build. I wrote the directory lookup as Key={'email': ...} and built the fake directory keyed on 'email' too. The battery passed 22/22 on a call that could never have worked against the real table (keyed PK='USER#<email>' / SK='PROFILE'). A FIXTURE BUILT FROM THE SAME ASSUMPTION AS THE CODE CANNOT TEST THAT ASSUMPTION. Found by measuring the live table rather than by reading my own code; fixed by rebuilding the stub from the MEASURED schema and then re-running the original bug as a mutant, which now fails exactly the enrichment check.

THE FIELD THE TO ASKED FOR DOES NOT EXIST. opal-users-v2 carries no user_id attribute at all (measured attribute set recorded in the Rule-24 record). user_id is filled with the row's actual primary key, and the redundancy with email is NAMED for the gate rather than quietly resolved.

TWO DEFECTS THAT WOULD HAVE FAILED THE SAME INVISIBLE WAY. A missing IAM grant and a wrong key shape both produce a blank claimer name, which is ALSO the correct rendering for a user genuinely absent from the directory -- semantically valid, not merely silent. That composition is what WA-10 exists to break, and it is why the two degradation tokens had to differ mechanically rather than in prose.
